candidates.name: Azure Throttling pattern
candidates.reason: Bound event-reporting request rates and bursts before they consume scarce API-server resources, with separate limits for noisy reporters.
candidates.application_scope: Reporter admission and aggregate API write budget.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: A per-reporter cap alone does not cap cluster-wide traffic; expose suppression counts and preserve representative application diagnostics.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened page explicitly last updated 2026-05-30; no earlier version verified.

candidates.name: Enterprise Integration Patterns — Aggregator
candidates.reason: Define the grouping key, flush condition, and summary algorithm explicitly so repeated failures can become understandable event series with fewer writes.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Bound groups and memory; retain meaningful message distinctions, counts, and timing instead of merging all similar-looking failures.
candidates.date_evidence: Authors' bibliography (https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/books1.html) dates the original 65-pattern collection to 2003; current wording is unversioned.

candidates.name: zap structured logging and duplicate sampling
candidates.reason: Use zap's error-flood sampling rationale and typed event fields as concrete examples of lowering reporting overhead while preserving readable context.
candidates.application_scope: Message classification and reporting hot path.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Its message-based duplicate identification may combine different field values; Kubernetes grouping needs an explicit semantic key and visible suppression.
candidates.date_evidence: Live README and FAQ provide no verified cutoff-compatible version.

candidates.name: zerolog structured events, sampling, and nonblocking output
candidates.reason: Borrow typed context fields, microsecond timestamp formatting, burst sampling, and bounded nonblocking output to make event production precise and inexpensive.
candidates.application_scope: Event envelope and producer-side reporter implementation.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Sampling loses occurrences; account for drops, enforce unique field names, and keep the API write limit separate from logger throughput.
candidates.date_evidence: Live README is undated; example timestamps do not prove feature publication dates.

candidates.name: Enterprise Integration Patterns — Idempotent Receiver
candidates.reason: Separate retransmission deduplication from repeated real occurrences so retries do not inflate counts and changed event meaning is not discarded.
candidates.application_scope: Event identity, retry semantics, and deduplication.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Delivery identity and semantic grouping identity serve different purposes; bounded deduplication state still needs restart and expiry rules.
candidates.date_evidence: Authors' bibliography (https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/books1.html) dates the original 65-pattern collection to 2003; current wording is unversioned.

candidates.name: Azure Queue-Based Load Leveling pattern
candidates.reason: Decouple event creation from API writes with a bounded reporter buffer drained at a controlled rate to absorb brief scheduling-failure bursts.
candidates.application_scope: Producer buffering and asynchronous write scheduling.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Use only a bounded local-buffer adaptation within scope; sustained overload requires coalescing or dropping, and crashes can lose buffered events.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened page explicitly last updated 2026-06-12; no earlier version verified.

candidates.name: Azure Circuit Breaker pattern
candidates.reason: Suspend repeated failing event writes and use limited recovery probes so reporting does not intensify an API-server outage.
candidates.application_scope: Event sink failure handling and retry suppression.
candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Set bounded timeouts and probes; do not recursively report every reporting failure, and make diagnostic gaps visible after recovery.
candidates.date_evidence: Opened page explicitly last updated 2025-03-21; no earlier version verified.

raw_response:
# C05 — catalogue baseline B

I found nine useful references. The applications below are my translations of the sources into this event-reporting problem; none has been tested or shown useful in Kubernetes by this run. The proposed scope remains event semantics and reporting behavior, with etcd persistence and existing retention unchanged.

## Candidates

1. **[Azure Throttling pattern](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/throttling)** — Bound reporter rates and bursts before event traffic exhausts API-server capacity. Combine reporter fairness with an aggregate write budget; local limits alone cannot bound a growing cluster. Preserve representative diagnostics and report suppressed counts. **Date: later evidence**, because the opened page was updated on 2026-05-30. Discovered through the [Azure catalogue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/).

2. **[EIP Aggregator](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/Aggregator.html)** — Make correlation, completion, and summarization explicit when collapsing repeated failures into event series. A bounded grouping table and timed flush can reduce writes while retaining counts and timing; message changes that alter meaning must remain distinguishable. **Date: core pattern available by 2003**, supported by the authors' bibliography; the live page's newer implementation examples are not used. Discovered through the [EIP catalogue](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html).

3. **[zap](https://github.com/uber-go/zap)** — Its [sampling rationale](https://github.com/uber-go/zap/blob/master/FAQ.md) directly addresses logging that worsens an error flood, while typed context fields separate readable text from machine-readable detail. Transfer the mechanism carefully: message-based duplicate identification can suppress entries whose fields differ, so the event design needs a deliberate semantic grouping key and suppression visibility. **Date: unknown**; the opened live documentation does not establish these features at the cutoff. Discovered through [awesome-go](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avelino/awesome-go/master/README.md).

4. **[zerolog](https://github.com/rs/zerolog)** — Provides a concrete example of typed event fields, configurable microsecond timestamp representation, burst sampling, and bounded nonblocking output. These mechanisms can inform the producer path; they do not themselves protect the API server. Track drops, prevent duplicate field names, and retain useful diagnostic representatives. **Date: unknown**. The attempted nanosecond-identifier lookup had no match, so I make no nanosecond claim. Discovered through [awesome-go](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avelino/awesome-go/master/README.md).

5. **[EIP Idempotent Receiver](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/IdempotentReceiver.html)** — Define how a retry of the same report differs from another real occurrence before choosing deduplication behavior. Delivery identity can prevent retry inflation, while a separate semantic grouping identity preserves changed meaning. Deduplication state must remain bounded and have explicit restart/expiry behavior. **Date: core pattern available by 2003**. Discovered through the [EIP catalogue](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html).

6. **[Azure Queue-Based Load Leveling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/queue-based-load-leveling)** — A bounded producer buffer drained at a controlled rate can absorb brief bursts without blocking application work on event writes. Sustained overload still needs coalescing or dropping, with an explicit loss policy. This is a local-buffer adaptation; adopting the page's durable broker architecture would exceed the stated persistence boundary. **Date: later evidence**, page updated 2026-06-12. Discovered through the [Azure catalogue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/).

7. **[Azure Circuit Breaker](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/circuit-breaker)** — Stop repeated event-write attempts when the API endpoint is failing and allow only limited recovery probes. Choose bounded timeouts and avoid emitting another event for every reporting failure; after recovery, explain diagnostic gaps. This complements admission limits rather than replacing them. **Date: later evidence**, page updated 2025-03-21. Discovered through the [Azure catalogue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/).

8. **[EIP Selective Consumer](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/MessageSelector.html)** — Stable producer-supplied selection fields offer an analogue for querying grouped events by application, object, reason, and reporter. Define those fields independently of human-readable prose. The pattern does not supply an etcd index or authorization model; query cost and access rules remain implementation work. **Date: core pattern available by 2003**. Discovered through the [EIP catalogue](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html).

9. **[EIP Event Message](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/EventMessage.html)** — Use the distinction between an occurrence and its delivery to clarify event meaning and timestamp fields. Its emphasis on timeliness also helps frame how much delivery effort is justified during overload. Preserve enough contextual detail for debugging, and specify what each time measures; this pattern does not provide a timestamp wire format. **Date: core pattern available by 2003**. Discovered through the [EIP catalogue](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html).

## Combined direction and limits

The most coherent combination is a typed event envelope, a documented semantic grouping rule, bounded reporter state, explicit suppression accounting, and a hard write budget. Selection fields should survive grouping so developers can still retrieve their application's events. Buffering and circuit breaking address different failure conditions and must share the same resource limits.

For date classification, the [authors' bibliography](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/books1.html) identifies the original EIP collection as Addison-Wesley, 2003 and says it contains the site's 65 patterns. That supports the core patterns' prior availability, not every sentence or modern example on today's pages. Azure pages remain later evidence; undated tool documentation remains unknown.

This internal separate-context run used GPT-6 Astra Pro, not a human translator or a different model. It used five catalogue-restricted search queries and 25 conservatively counted source accesses: 19 open/click attempts plus six in-page finds, including rereads and the no-match lookup. Every candidate has an opened discovery listing and opened verification source. No recognized target-proposal exposure occurred; prior model memory cannot be controlled. No implementation, benchmark, deployment, or usefulness claim is made.

budget.limit: 25 source accesses or 20 minutes; conservative access count includes all rereads and finds

Searches were restricted to allowed catalogues/lists; off-query snippets appeared but were not followed for discovery. No recognized target-proposal exposure was observed, and pretraining memory leakage cannot be erased.
All primary verification followed opened permitted catalogue listings. External primary pages were used only to verify the already discovered candidates, not to discover additional candidates.
EIP core-pattern availability is supported by the authors' 2003 bibliographic entry; current pages themselves are unversioned and modern examples were not relied on.

Azure verification pages explicitly carry 2025 or 2026 update dates and are retained as post-decision evidence. Tool documentation remains date-unknown; example timestamps and catalogue update dates were not used to backdate tool features.

The first multi-page retrieval returned titles without substantive text for several sources, requiring recorded rereads. Page-access budgeting conservatively includes those rereads and all six find operations.
The TimeFormatUnixNano lookup returned no match on an opened page. Microsecond formatting was verified; nanosecond support was not.
